title: Reduce Console Aggregator Contention via per-tenant request lanes and TTL harmonization
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: The console API aggregation layer exhibits frequent p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional 5xx bursts under tenant concurrency (esp. dashboards and route /v1/console/list). Root causes identified: (1) unbounded resolver concurrency in the GraphQL aggregator that causes hot-path CPU/heap contention, (2) inconsistent TTLs across cache adapters (redis vs in-process prefix cache) leading to stampedes and duplicated upstream fetches, and (3) legacy batching windows tuned for older load profiles that increase amplification during spikes.

Goal: Reduce tail latency and error bursts by introducing per-tenant request lanes (lightweight concurrency limiter per customer/route), centralizing KV-cache coordination to serialize cache fills for hot keys, harmonizing TTLs across adapters and introducing jittered revalidation, and a minimal GraphQL resolver middleware rewrite to allow cooperative yielding and early-response fastpaths. Deliverables are incremental and feature-flagged with canary rollouts and clear guardrails.

Constraints/Non-goals: We will not replace the entire aggregation pipeline or introduce a new sidecar service in this ticket; the cache coordinator should be implemented as an in-process coordinator with an option to extract to a small service in a later ticket if needed. We will not change public API contracts.

Success metrics (staging benchmarks): p95 latency for dashboard listing route down >=30%, p99 down >=20%, tail 5xx rate reduced >=60% under synthetic tenant hot-spot tests, and <=10% infra cost delta post-rollout.

Approach summary: 1) Add per-route/per-tenant concurrency limiter (configurable via Console config) with token-bucket semantics and soft-fallback to degraded-but-successful responses. 2) Implement KV-cache coordinator: single-flight style promise coalescing with a bounded queue and timebox for backend fetches; unify cache adapters to honor coordinator TTLs and introduce jittered TTL expiry to avoid stampedes. 3) GraphQL resolver middleware: cooperative yielding for long-running resolver chains, shorten default batching window for identified routes, and add metrics for contention, queue length, and coordinator hit/miss. 4) Instrumentation: add per-tenant lane metrics, coordinator metrics, and SLO dashboards for canary evaluation. 5) Run dependency upgrade CI job to ensure no regressions with graphql-js 17.x and apollo-server 4.x in a separate subtask.
acceptance_criteria: p95 end-to-end latency for the dashboard listing route on staging reduced by >= 30% compared to baseline run
tail error rate (5xx/timeout) during synthetic high-concurrency tenant tests reduced by >= 60%
integration tests cover cache-coordinator single-flight behavior, coordinator timeouts, and per-route concurrency fallback
canary rollout automation (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with rollback triggers implemented in console-deploy
no user-facing API changes and feature flags available to disable new behaviors

2026-02-28 - Diego Martinez: PoC for per-tenant token-bucket limiter implemented in console/aggregator/limiter (branch: feat/limiter-poC). Microbenchmarks show limiter adds ~0.4ms median overhead but prevents queue growth under load.
2026-03-02 - Review feedback from Lina Chen (Platform SRE): ensure coordinator backpressure surfaced to request tracing and add graceful degradation (serve stale cache when backend times out).

2026-03-04 - Diego Martinez: Implemented KV-cache coordinator (single-flight) in-memory with pluggable Redis-lock fallback. Added unit tests for race conditions and timeouts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/14681

2026-03-06 - PM review (Ravi Patel): confirm rollout plan and success metrics. Agreed to canary at 5% then 25% then full. Documented rollback triggers: >20% regression in p95 or >10% increase in 5xx for canary cohort.

2026-03-08 - QA (Nora Singh): running stress harness with 100 concurrent tenants hitting hot keys. Early results: coordinator reduces duplicate fetches by 78% and peak CPU by ~18%. Need to tighten TTL harmonization.

2026-03-10 - Diego Martinez: TTL harmonizer implemented — TTL config now centralized in console/cache/config and adapters read unified TTL + jitter. Benchmarks attached in PR. Next: scheduling canary rollout and add SLO dashboard panels.
